tei:div.tei:p: This is a Passover adaptation of “Marching through Georgia” (1865) by Henry Clay Work (1832-1884). “Marching through Georgia” is a somewhat controversial song for two reasons, one of them valid, the other (in my opinion) not as much. The valid problem: the second verse of the original text features a racial slur. When people sing it now we skip or replace that line. The less valid problem: pity for the poor Confederate plantation owners whose homes were destroyed by Sherman’s forces. I frankly do not care about the suffering of slavers in a slave state. I shed no tears for the monsters who enforced the inhuman system of chattel slavery, and I treat their homes’ destruction as the just deserts of their sin in owning human beings as property.
